prairie dog, black-tailed prairie dog ( Cynomys ludovicianus).
spring peeper, chorus frog, tree frog (Pseudacris spp. and Hyla spp.).
sonny; daughter, an appelative for a young person, male or female .

in cold, frigid, freezing weather; in winter, during winter, during winter-time.
his, their brother; her, their sister; my, our brother (of male), my, our sister (of female).

"Man Going East" or "Man Going Downstream." The first independent Southern Band, given birth by someone 's religious vision. Known as Tap-age (noisy) by the French on account of their "pentecostal" type of early morning prayers.
son, sonny, a term of address for a child that indicates he is acting in a childish manner.
your nephew; your niece (man's sister's child).
sibling of same sex: brother (of male), sister (of female).
half; in the middle, in the center.
half of; part, piece, portion, share of.
dwarf plum (Prunus sp., Astragalus sp.?), grows about one-and-a-half feet high and has small fruit.
fox (generic) (Gray Fox, Urocyon cinereoargenteus and Red Fox, Vulpes vulpes).
coyote (Canis latrans), wolf (Canis lupus lycaon); Coyote, the trickster.
prairie chicken (gen.) (incl. Tympanuchus spp. and Centrocercus urophasianus).
mink (Mustela vison); water dog, a legendary aquatic animal noted for its ferocity and healing powers.
toothed-edge scraper of bison leg bone, used as a flesher.
cradleboard cloth used to wrap an infant ; the cloth is attached to the cradleboard and holds the baby on the board as well as shields its head.
cooked food, esp. bread and meat.
cooked food, as bread or meat .

vine; bush, as a berry or rose bush.
robe, of either buffalo or bear, with the fur remaining on it .
pendant; hanging or dangling object used to decorate clothing , as a cowry shell .
dry goods, as cloth, calico, material, linens, blankets.
straw, as used for baskets and hats.
fuzz, light coat of fur, short hair; stubble.
"Little Mud Lodge Village." Or, perhaps "Little Swamp" from kit-kaharu ' , swamp, slough. Known in early literature as "Republican Pawnee," for the river where the villages were.
dry native grass, formerly used as a floor cover; hay, as used for horse feed.
buckskin horse; light-colored horse with a black mane and tail.
buckskin horse with dark mane and tail and a black nose.
red paint; vermilion; red ocher, as used for ritual painting of the body and objects.
black pepper; bell pepper; chili pepper.
white clay, as used for painting the body in rituals .
tin pail, tin kettle; white pail, white kettle.
night, as a period of a night and day that elapses when counting time; equivalent to English reckoning by days .
night, as a period of a night and day that elapses when counting time; equivalent of Western reckoning by days .
dawn twilight, first light of day on the horizon.
Ohio River or "something's always floating down"
Loup River , a fork of the Platte River (central Nebraska).
ravine, gully, gulch, draw, washout, as one created by a stream; dry creek; small ditch.

pieces of meat hanging to dry, pieces of hanging dried meat.
false indigo, water string ( Amorpha fruticosa ).
cold water; spring water; well water.
pond, lake, slough, body of water; area of standing water.
seed in the women's plum seed game.
cornbread with a bean filling, i.e., a combination of cornmeal and beans.
joint grass, tall native grass that is jointed.
bearberry bush (Arctostaphylos uva-ursi), the leaves of which were used for smoking.
red osier, red dogwood, kinnikinnick (Cornus amomum), the inner bark of which was used for tobacco.
corn on a cob, unshelled corn; ear of corn.
kettle, pot , as for cooking; bucket, pail.
elk antler scraper, a curved antler handle with a blade (of flint or steel) attached to the end .
paunch, as used for a water pouch .
row of hills, as mounds in which garden seeds are planted.
little wild sage, prairie sagewort (Artemisia frigida).
flat reed; heavy, coarse green marsh grass, as used for weaving mats .
sod, turf; chunk of mud or earth; dirt clod.
flat or level ground : level clearing , meadow, small level valley, bottom land, low level area; valley floor; flat, flat field; prairie.
like, care for, have an affinity for.
brave, warrior; brave or valorous man.

be vain, proud, as someone who is a show-off or who dresses ostentatiously or fastidiously; be conceited.
fear, have fear of, be afraid of.
shake, quiver, tremble, shiver, as when cold or angry.
be stubborn, obstinate; be intractable, recalcitrant.

be outstanding, extraordinary, exceptional, as a warrior who stands out above others.
be together, always together, as companions.

Skiri tribe; Loup tribe, Wolf tribe.

be named, called; be one's name.
be named after; have someone's name.
call, summon, as when inviting someone.
get into water, lie down in water; go down in water, as a bird diving.
crawl, crawl on one's hands and knees; crawl to.
string, cord, twine, thong , as used for a belt or to hold or carry something .

again; back, as to come back or return to a starting point.
come; (idiom) be here, said when someone has arrived.

throat, front part of the neck.
chest, breast; area of clavicle, collarbone.
